subject: Budget range validation & pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@paybridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Budget range validation & pricing follow-up

Thanks again for the time this morning - really helpful to learn more about PayBridge's roadmap for AI-powered underwriting. Quick recap and two asks so we can get a tailored commercial proposal ready: 

Recap (what I heard)
- Pilot (Q2): 20-140M tokens/month, primarily batch scoring of loan applications (short prompts, ~120 tokens/request).
- Production (6 months): 80-120M tokens/month as you roll out scoring to more product lanes and add conversational flows.
- Key must-haves: SOC 2 evidence, DPA, ability to invoice monthly, PO process (procurement thresholds), and predictability on unit cost.

Asks
1) Can you confirm the budget band PayBridge is targeting for the pilot and production phases (monthly spend)? e.g., pilot $X-$Y / month, production $A-$B / month.
2) What procurement thresholds/requirements should we plan for? (e.g., minimum PO size, contract review timeline, net terms)

To make the math explicit for procurement, what target $/1M tokens should we use? For example, if you target $900 / 1M tokens, 50M tokens would imply ~$45k/month. If you target $600 / 1M tokens, that would be ~$30k/month. Knowing the target lets us model both hosted and committed pricing options.

Attaching the Redwood pricing deck and a short example calc sheet - I'll follow up with a worked example once you confirm the target $/1M and procurement rules.

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-deck.pdf (pricing + committed discounts), sample-token-calculator.xlsx (referenced inline)

Next steps
- If you can reply with the budget band and procurement thresholds today/tomorrow, I'll put together a proposal and a two-option pricing page (hosted vs committed).

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: (415) 555-0123 | dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Thanks for the clear recap, Dylan - that matches what we discussed. A few specifics from procurement and finance: 

Estimated volumes (internal planning)
- Pilot (next 60 days): 20-140M tokens/month.
- Ramp (3-6 months): 50-80M tokens/month.
- Production (6-12 months): 80-120M tokens/month (depends on adoption).

Budget bands (what execs are comfortable with)
- Pilot: $8k-$25k/month.
- Ramp: $25k-$55k/month.
- Production: $55k-$120k/month.

Target unit economics
- Leadership is expecting an execution price in the ballpark of $750-$950 per 1M tokens (they understand this varies by model and commitment level). That gives the ranges above.

Procurement thresholds / requirements
- Minimum PO size: $25,000 (anything below can go on a credit card).
- Contract review: procurement needs a SOW + standard MSP terms; legal review can take up to 3 weeks for new vendors.
- Payment terms: 60 days net preferred; they will accept 30 days for enterprise contracts.

Compliance
- Please provide SOC 2 Type II report and a DPA. Procurement specifically asked for data residency notes (we are US-based).

Procurement contact: procurement@paybridge.com (Elena will handle the intake).

If you can send a worked example showing 3 scenarios (hosted pay-as-you-go, 12-month committed at a 20% discount, and dedicated/reserved pricing), we'll review with finance next week.

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Head of Product | PayBridge
sam@paybridge.com

Appreciate the detail, Sam - that's super helpful. I put together a short worked example below (quick math) and attached the pricing deck + a draft SOW for procurement.

Worked example (illustrative)
- Assumptions: 300 tokens per interaction average (prompt + generation), 1,000,000 interactions => 300M tokens.
- Example volumes: 50M tokens/month = 166k interactions/month (50,000,000 / 300).

Cost scenarios (using your target band)
- If target is $750 / 1M tokens: 50M => $37,500 / month.
- If target is $900 / 1M tokens: 50M => $45,000 / month.
- If target is $950 / 1M tokens: 50M => $47,500 / month.

Committed option idea (12-mo)
- We can model a committed discount (example): 20% off hosted list for a 12-month commit at projected volumes. For 50M tokens, that would move $45k -> $36k at a $900 base (example). We'll show committed tiers so finance can see the delta vs pay-as-you-go.

Next steps
1) I'll produce a 1-page commercial summary with three options (hosted payg, 12-mo commit, dedicated/reserved) and a simple token-to-dollar calc.
2) Neha - can you add recommended discount tiers for a 6- and 12-month commit? Also flag any limits on offering sub-$700/1M publicly.
3) Sam/Elena - once we have the 1-pager I'll include the SOW and SOC2 link for procurement.

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-deck.pdf, SOW-draft-paybridge.docx

Best,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
